ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $\odot O$. If $\angle BOD = 100^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle DCB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\because \angle BOD=100^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAD=\frac{1}{2}\angle BOD=50^\circ$;\\
Since $\because \angle BAD+\angle BCD=180^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BCD=180^\circ-\angle BAD=180^\circ-50^\circ=\boxed{130^\circ}$.

B is at the lower left, D is on the right, and C is on the shorter arc from B to D; the radii OB and OD are drawn in the figure, therefore ∠BOD is a central angle. Reasoning: It is known that ∠BOD = 100°, and a central angle is equal to the measure of the minor arc BD that it subtends, so minor arc BD = 100°. Because point C is located on minor arc BD, the arc subtended by ∠DCB is the other arc BD that does not contain C, namely major arc BD, whose measure is 360° - 100° = 260°. According to the inscribed angle theorem, an inscribed angle is equal to half the measure of the arc it subtends, so ∠DCB = 260° / 2 = 130°.
